healthcareSystem: Mixed public-private system. Princess Margaret Hospital in Nassau is the main public facility. Private clinics in Nassau and Freeport cater to tourists. Out Islands have very limited medical facilities.
qualityNotes: Decent private healthcare in Nassau and Freeport. Doctors Hospital is the top private facility. Out Islands have only basic clinics. English is spoken everywhere. For serious conditions, patients are evacuated to Miami.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies open 9am-6pm weekdays, 9am-1pm Saturday. Limited Sunday hours.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies in Nassau and Freeport are well-stocked. Out Islands have very limited pharmacy access — bring all medications with you. All staff speak English. Prices are higher than the US.
prescriptionRules: Most prescription medications require a valid prescription. Controlled substances strictly regulated. English-speaking country so communication is straightforward.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Carry a doctor's letter and keep medications in original packaging.

restrictedMeds.name: Cannabis products
restrictedMeds.note: Cannabis is illegal in The Bahamas. Do not bring CBD or THC products.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all prescription medications. Keep medications in original labeled containers. English documentation is accepted.

travelInsurance.tips: Strongly recommended. Medical evacuation to Miami is common for serious cases and costs $25,000-50,000 without insurance. Ensure coverage includes water sports and boating activities.

vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations for most travelers. Yellow fever certificate required if arriving from an endemic country.

waterNotes: Tap water is generally safe in Nassau, Paradise Island, and Freeport resorts. On Out Islands, bottled water is recommended. Resort water is treated and safe to drink.
foodSafetyTips: Food at restaurants and resorts is generally safe. Conch (national dish) should be fresh. Be cautious with roadside fish fry vendors — stick to busy, popular ones. Avoid raw shellfish from unregulated sources.
medicalTourismNote: The Bahamas is not a medical tourism destination. For specialized treatment, patients travel to Miami (35-minute flight from Nassau).
metaDescription: Health guide for The Bahamas: emergency numbers, pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccinations, safe tap water, and insurance advice.

hospitals.name: Doctors Hospital
hospitals.notes: Best private hospital in The Bahamas. Modern facility, 24/7 emergency department. Preferred by tourists and expats.

hospitals.name: Princess Margaret Hospital
hospitals.notes: Main public hospital. Emergency department can be busy. Largest hospital in the country.

hospitals.name: Rand Memorial Hospital
hospitals.notes: Main hospital for Grand Bahama Island. Public facility with emergency services.

hospitals.name: Walk-In Medical Clinic
hospitals.notes: Private clinic convenient for Cable Beach and resort area tourists.

pharmacyPhrases.local: I need medicine for a headache

dentalCare.availability: Dental care available in Nassau and Freeport. Limited on Out Islands.
dentalCare.notes: Private dental clinics in Nassau offer good quality care. All staff speak English.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Doctors Hospital has dental referral services. Several private dental practices near Bay Street in Nassau.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Available in Nassau. English is the official language.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services limited but available through private practitioners in Nassau. Sandilands Rehabilitation Centre is the main psychiatric facility.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility is improving but inconsistent. Major resorts generally have accessible facilities. Older buildings and Out Islands have limited accessibility.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Doctors Hospital and Princess Margaret Hospital have wheelchair access.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport (jitney buses). Taxis and resort shuttles may accommodate wheelchairs.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Atlantis Resort on Paradise Island has good accessibility. Confirm accessibility with specific hotels before booking. Beach wheelchairs available at some resorts.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: Available at hospitals and clinics in Nassau and Freeport.
covidStatus.notes: Hurricane season (June-November), sun exposure, and marine-related injuries are more relevant health concerns.

insuranceClaimProcess: Private hospitals require upfront payment (cash or credit card, USD accepted). Keep all receipts and medical reports for insurance claims. English documentation provided.

commonCosts.note: Estimated typical out-of-pocket costs at private facilities. The Bahamas uses the Bahamian Dollar (pegged 1:1 to USD). US dollars accepted everywhere.

medicalEvacuation.note: Miami is only a 35-minute flight from Nassau. Air ambulance services are well-established. Out Island evacuations may require two-stage transport (local plane to Nassau, then to Miami).

drugNameMap.note: US brands dominate. Both Tylenol and generic acetaminophen widely available.
